label: Text detachment
summary: Text detachment is the practice of not emotionally over-identifying with your own writing, so that feedback does not feel like a personal attack. It means treating your content as a product with quality parameters that can be discussed and adjusted, rather than as an extension of your ego. In Maaike's framework, text detachment counters the emotional labor that feedback can trigger, and it is a prerequisite for building genuine feedback resilience.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike frames text detachment as a skill that develops with experience and deliberate practice, not a personality trait you either have or don't. She points to concrete techniques that support it, like taking written notes during feedback conversations, which occupy enough mental bandwidth to crowd out defensive emotional reactions. She also ties detachment to a broader reframe: your job is to deliver something that meets your client's goals, full stop. The more you write and build routine around the craft, the less any single text feels existential, which makes detachment progressively easier to sustain.
open_questions: The post gestures at a practical follow-up but the reference is cut off, so it is unclear what specific tools or frameworks Maaike links to text detachment in that follow-on piece.

Maaike mentions that the success of your work depends partly on context and other people, but does not resolve how to stay detached when external factors genuinely do undermine a project rather than just feeling that way.
